source_text:
Περίψημα τὸ ἐμὸν πνεῦμα τοῦ σταυροῦ, ὅ ἐστιν σκάνδαλον τοῖς ἀπιστοῦσιν, ἡμῖν δὲ σωτηρία καὶ ζωὴ αἰώνιος, ποῦ σοφός; ποῦ συζητητής; ποῦ καύχησις τῶν λεγομένων συνετῶν;
ὁ γὰρ θεὸς ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦς ὁ Χριστὸς ἐκυοφορήθη ὑπὸ Μαρίας κατ’ οἰκονομίαν θεοῦ ἐκ σπέρματος μὲν Δαυείδ, πνεύματος δὲ ἁγίου: ὃς ἐγεννήθη καὶ ἐβαπτίσθη, ἵνα τῷ πάθει τὸ ὕδωρ καθαρίσῃ.
thought_title: The Cross as Wisdom and the Incarnation of Jesus
orientation: Ignatius, writing to the Ephesians, is contrasting the cross as the true wisdom of God with the empty wisdom of the world, and then states the incarnation and baptism of Jesus.
pass_a_gloss: An offscouring [is] my spirit of the cross, which is a stumbling block to the ones disbelieving, but to us salvation and life eternal. Where [is] a wise [one]? Where [is] a disputer? Where [is] the boasting of the ones called intelligent? For our God Jesus the Christ was carried in the womb by Mary according to the plan of God, from seed on the one hand of David, but of spirit on the other hand holy; who was born and was baptized, in order that by the passion (capable of suffering) he might purify the water.

choices.why: Literal sense of refuse or scum, matching the Greek noun's meaning of something wiped off or cast away; preserves the stark self-deprecation Ignatius uses of his spirit in relation to the cross.

choices.english: according to the plan of God
choices.why: The phrase denotes God's ordered arrangement or dispensation; 'plan' captures the deliberate divine purpose without importing later theological terms.
rejected: according to the economy of God

choices.term: ἐκ σπέρματος μὲν Δαυείδ, πνεύματος δὲ ἁγίου
choices.english: from seed on the one hand of David, but of spirit on the other hand holy
choices.why: The μὲν...δὲ construction sets up a contrast between the human descent from David and the divine origin from the Holy Spirit; the literal rendering preserves the balanced antithesis.
rejected: from the seed of David and from the Holy Spirit
descended from David and from the Holy Spirit

choices.term: ἵνα τῷ πάθει τὸ ὕδωρ καθαρίσῃ
choices.english: in order that by the passion he might purify the water
choices.why: The purpose clause is rendered literally with 'in order that' and the subjunctive 'might purify' to show the intended result of the baptism; 'passion' is the fixed glossary term for πάθος.
rejected: so that through his suffering he might cleanse the water
to purify the water by his passion

pass_b_english: My spirit is an expiation of the cross, which is a stumbling block to those who disbelieve, but to us it is salvation and eternal life. Where is the wise person? Where is the debater? Where is the boasting of those called intelligent?

For our God, Jesus the Christ, was carried in the womb by Mary according to the plan of God, from the seed of David on the one hand, but of the Holy Spirit on the other. He was born and baptized so that by his passion he might purify the water.

last_rejected.why: Glossary term πάθος = 'passion', not used; but main issue: 'offscouring' obscures meaning.
last_rejected.fix: My spirit is the scum/waste of the cross
last_rejected.ruling: Περίψημα means 'offscouring'; archaic but accurate. No meaning changed or lost.

last_rejected.quote: by his passion he might purify the water
last_rejected.source_quote: ἵνα τῷ πάθει τὸ ὕδωρ καθαρίσῃ
last_rejected.why: τῷ πάθει is dative of means/instrument, not agent; 'by his passion' misrepresents grammar.
last_rejected.fix: so that the water might be purified by the passion
last_rejected.ruling: τῷ πάθει is dative of means; 'by his passion' correctly renders instrumental dative. No misrepresentation.

problems.why: 'Passible' (capable of suffering) vs 'passion' (suffering/death) are related but distinct; reader may miss Christological point.
problems.fix: Gloss 'passible' as 'capable of suffering' on first use.

problems.quote: Where is the wise person? Where is the debater?
problems.why: Alludes to 1 Cor 1:20 but not exact quotation; reader may not recognize allusion.

problems.quote: My spirit is the offscouring of the cross
problems.why: Same archaic term; combined with 'of the cross' the phrase is opaque.
problems.fix: Use 'My spirit is devoted to the cross' or 'My spirit is the refuse of the cross.'

fixed: The 'passible' problem is not in the English text; the English uses 'passion,' which is the correct glossary term. I added a clarifying gloss in the literal gloss instead.
The scripture allusion is not a wrong citation; the English does not cite a verse. I left the text as is.
The 'offscouring' problem was real; I changed it to 'refuse' for clarity.

problems.quote: My spirit is the refuse of the cross
problems.why: 'Refuse' seems wrong; the Greek likely means 'expiation' or 'offering.'

problems.quote: He was born and baptized so that by his passion he might purify the water.
problems.why: Theology is that Jesus sanctified baptismal water by his passion; 'purify the water' may mislead as literal water purification.
problems.fix: Consider 'sanctify the waters [of baptism]' with note.

problems.quote: Where is the wise person? Where is the debater? Where is the boasting of those called intelligent?
